newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares head for correction next week-charts.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares head for correction next week-charts.

text.p: Russia's bullish share market has stumbled recently, but technical analysts said on Wednesday it may have another week or so to run higher before a more serious downward correction sets in.
"The RTS index could rise to 525-545 before profit taking," said MC Securities Technical Analyst Mark Kane in London. "A classical trend line suggests resistance around that level."

The 22-share index of leading shares closed at 503.37 on Wednesday, breaking the 500 level for the second time in three days after a month-long rise which saw the index of leading liquid shares soar from 360 in early June.
"Right about this area people are going to start taking profits, probably in the next 10 days," Kane said.
CentreInvest Securities technical analyst Lauri Sillandaka said the index would have trouble around 500. "Five hundred is a big number -- it is a psychological resistance level."

He predicted the market would continue its rise to make a double peak, repeating a Russian market trend. The market made a double-peak around last year's presidential election before a summer bear market set in.
"In Russia, the market tends to autocorrelate with past performance," he said.
He said a 10 percent drop from Tuesday's close of 504.55 was possible, and a five percent correction likely.
"I think there will be a downward correction next week and then I see it going up though 500. When it breaks that I see it going up to 600 in the next two months."
The gap between long- and short-term moving averages has widened to levels not seen in a year -- suggesting the market is rising too fast and needs to cool off.
"That is another pointer that the market is due for a bit of profit-taking," Kane said, although he added such averages were generally too sophisticated for the Russian emerging market.
But the analysts differed on predictions for the summer market.
Sillandaka said trend lines and Elliott waves indicated a summer rally. Trend lines linking peaks and troughs on a graph of market closes are extended to forecast future caps for growth and decline.
Elliott waves forecast cycles of buying and selling based on the duration and performance of previous cycles.
But Kane said that his trend line analysis indicated the market would fall over the summer by up to 15-20 percent from current levels and revive only in the autumn.

"There may be a pullback to the 450 level, but this could take three months," he said. "It will not be a sudden drop but a slow drift. Everything is right -- the time of year, the (previous) bull market phrases, the trend lines."
He said the pickup would begin in the autumn.
"There is still another move to come."
